skill.name: web-search
skill.description: Adds web search and page extraction workflows through inference.sh apps for Tavily and Exa. It covers search answers, URL extraction, source gathering, and RAG-oriented research.
skill.summary: Search and extract web content with Tavily and Exa through the inference.sh CLI.
skill.author: inference-sh

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are Markdown backticks around examples and app identifiers, so they are false positives. The audit confirms the line 20 pipe-to-shell installer and its installer URL as real risks that must be removed or replaced.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly into sh.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the curl-to-shell command with a signed package, checksum verification, or a link to manual installation instructions.

remediation.issue: Search, extraction, and LLM workflows send data to external services.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users that queries, URLs, extracted text, and prompts may leave their environment.

remediation.issue: Shell examples mix installation, search, extraction, and related-skill commands.
remediation.suggestion: Separate installation guidance from runtime examples and require explicit user confirmation before running commands.

content.user_title: Search the Web with Tavily and Exa
content.value_statement: Research tasks need current sources and clean page content. This skill uses inference.sh with Tavily and Exa to search, extract, and summarize web material.
actual_capabilities: Run Tavily search assistant queries through the inference.sh CLI.
Extract clean text and images from one or more public URLs.
Run Exa search for relevant links with context.
Ask Exa for direct factual answers.
Chain search or extraction results into LLM summarization workflows.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI and a logged-in account.
Depends on Tavily, Exa, and OpenRouter availability and terms.
Cannot guarantee source accuracy or freshness without user review.
May send queries, URLs, and extracted text to external services.

use_cases.title: Source Discovery
use_cases.description: Find current sources, links, and context for a topic before drafting a report.

use_cases.title: RAG Preparation
use_cases.description: Collect and extract public web pages for retrieval-augmented generation workflows.

use_cases.title: Claim Checking
use_cases.description: Search for supporting or conflicting evidence before publishing a factual claim.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Search
prompt_templates.scenario: Find a quick overview with sources.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search the web for recent sources about renewable energy storage. Return a short answer and source list.

prompt_templates.title: Extract One Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn a public page into clean content.
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract the main content from this public URL: [URL]. Summarize key points and include source metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Sources
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Tavily and Exa to research [topic]. Compare top sources, note disagreements, and cite the strongest evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Build Research Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare material for a RAG pipeline.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for [topic], extract the best pages, then prepare a RAG-ready brief with source quality notes.

output_examples.input: Search for recent AI safety regulation sources.
output_examples.output: A concise answer with relevant links, source titles, and short context for each result.

output_examples.input: Extract two public articles for a project brief.
output_examples.output: Clean article text, image references, and source details ready for summarization.

output_examples.input: Compare search results for a technical topic.
output_examples.output: A ranked source list with evidence notes, disagreements, and recommended follow-up reading.

best_practices: Review sources before using answers in decisions.
Use public URLs and avoid secrets in queries.
Prefer extraction for specific pages and search for broad discovery.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote installers into a shell without verification.
Do not send confidential documents through third-party extraction.
Do not treat generated answers as citations without checking sources.

faq.question: Does this skill browse the web directly?
faq.answer: It runs inference.sh apps for Tavily and Exa when the user asks for search or extraction.

faq.question: Which services does it use?
faq.answer: It documents Tavily Search, Tavily Extract, Exa Search, Exa Answer, and Exa Extract.

faq.question: Can it extract private pages?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for public URLs and depends on provider access rules.

faq.question: Does it need an account?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples assume the inference.sh CLI is installed and authenticated.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Should I send sensitive data?
faq.answer: Avoid sending secrets or private content because queries and URLs go to external services.
